hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 358 (Repeal and savings) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 358 (Repeal and savings), Chapter XX — Repeal and Savings.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (1) The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed
   (2) (2) Notwithstanding the repeal of the Code referred to in sub-section
   (3) (1), it shall not affect,—
   (4) (a) the previous operation of the Code so repealed or anything duly done or suffered thereunder; or
   (5) (b) any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the Code so repealed; or
   (6) (c) any penalty, or punishment incurred in respect of any offences committed against the Code so repealed; or
   (7) (d) any investigation or remedy in respect of any such penalty, or punishment; or
   (8) (e) any proceeding, investigation or remedy in respect of any such penalty or punishment as aforesaid, and any such proceeding or remedy may be instituted, continued or enforced, and any such penalty may be imposed as if that Code had not been repealed
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 358 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 358 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 358 (Repeal and savings)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 358 deals with Repeal and savings. It sits in Chapter XX — Repeal and Savings of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Repeal and savings. The Indian Penal Code, 1860 is repealed. Anything done, any right, privilege, obligation, liability, penalty or punishment under the IPC, and any investigation or proceeding in respect of an IPC offence, continues. Offences committed before 1 July 2024 are IPC offences.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 358 is the rule on “Repeal and savings”. The section provides that (1) The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. (1) The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed
2. (2) Notwithstanding the repeal of the Code referred to in sub-section
3. (1), it shall not affect,—
4. (a) the previous operation of the Code so repealed or anything duly done or suffered thereunder; or
5. (b) any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the Code so repealed; or
6. (c) any penalty, or punishment incurred in respect of any offences committed against the Code so repealed; or
7. (d) any investigation or remedy in respect of any such penalty, or punishment; or
8. (e) any proceeding, investigation or remedy in respect of any such penalty or punishment as aforesaid, and any such proceeding or remedy may be instituted, continued or enforced, and any such penalty may be imposed as if that Code had not been repealed

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 358. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Conclusion. BNS s. 358 is the complete current-law heading for Repeal and savings. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Complete statutory structure: introduction, meaning, ingredients, illustration, explanation/exception, application, and current-law citation.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. The IPC goes. Offences committed before 1 July 2024 stay under the old Code.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Analytical comment. Explain a condition, a proviso, or a practical difficulty in applying s. 358. Do not invent case names.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 358.”
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Exhaustive written submissions: foundational statutory note plus doctrinal contrast, second illustration or hypothetical, IRAC application, and current-law close.

cases.name: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
cases.holding: IPC 377 read down for consenting adults. BNS does not re-enact 377. Consensual same-sex intimacy is not an offence; non-consensual male rape is a legislative gap.

cases.name: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
cases.holding: Adultery (IPC 497) struck down. BNS does not revive it. Marital infidelity is not, by itself, a crime.

examTips: Cite BNS s. 358 for offences on or after 1 July 2024.
Ingredients first, illustration second, application third, conclusion last.
Date of the offence, not date of the FIR, decides IPC vs BNS on substance.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Formally repeals the Indian Penal Code, 1860 while ensuring legal continuity by saving pending investigations, trials, liabilities, and punishments.
statutoryFramework: Chapter XIX — Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult, Annoyance, Defamation, etc., and Repeal, BNS s. 358.

Core Legal Mandate: (1) The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed
(2) Notwithstanding the repeal of the Code referred to in sub-section (1), it shall not affect,—
(a) the previous operation of the Code so repealed or anyt...
Classification and Sentencing: Structured under Chapter XIX penal tiers.
Evidentiary and Procedural Cognate: Governed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
essentialIngredients: (1) The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed
(2) Notwithstanding the repeal of the Code referred to in sub-section
(a) the previous operation of the Code so repealed or anything duly done or suffered thereunder
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 358 is the concluding provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Sub-section (1) formally repeals the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860). Sub-section (2) establishes a comprehensive savings clause governing the transition from colonial to modern criminal law: the repeal shall not affect the previous operation of the IPC, any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired or incurred, any penalty or forfeiture incurred, or any investigation, legal proceeding, or remedy. All offences committed prior to 1 July 2024 continue to be investigated, inquired into, and tried under the IPC by virtue of Section 358 and Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, while offences committed on or after 1 July 2024 are governed by BNS.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of repeal and savings under Section 358 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 358.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 358 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: BNS s. 358 vs Article 20(1) Constitution: Article 20(1) bars retroactive criminal law; Section 358 ensures procedural and substantive continuity for past acts under the IPC.
Section 358 vs Section 531 BNSS: Section 358 saves substantive criminal liabilities under the IPC; Section 531 of BNSS saves procedural steps and pending trials under the CrPC.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 358 for conduct relating to repeal and savings.
Rule: Under BNS s. 358, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 358.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 358 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
